sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Barbell Back Squat is a fundamental compound exercise and one of the most effective movements for building overall lower body strength and mass.

With the barbell positioned across the upper back, this exercise targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings while also engaging the core and spinal erectors for stabilization.

Widely considered the king of all leg exercises, the barbell back squat is a staple in strength training, powerlifting, and athletic performance programs.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Builds exceptional lower body strength and power
- Increases muscle mass in the quads, glutes, and hamstrings
- Improves core stability and overall balance
- Enhances athletic performance across all sports
- Increases bone density and joint health
- Boosts testosterone and growth hormone production
- Develops functional movement patterns used in daily life

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus

Secondary: Hamstrings, Erector Spinae, Core, Adductors, Calves

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Position the barbell at upper chest height on the squat rack.
2. Step under the bar and position it across your upper back on your traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar).
3. Grip the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
4. Brace your core, lift the bar off the rack, and step back 2-3 steps.
5. Set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly outward (15-30 degrees).
6. Stand tall with your chest up and shoulders back.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Take a deep breath and brace your core.
2. Initiate the movement by breaking at the hips and knees simultaneously.
3. Lower your body in a controlled manner, keeping your chest up and back straight.
4. Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the ground.
5. Keep your knees tracking over your toes throughout the movement.
6. Drive through your mid-foot and heels to stand back up.
7. Exhale at the top and squeeze your glutes to complete the rep.
8. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Knees caving inward during the descent or ascent
- Rounding the lower back under load
- Not reaching proper depth (at least parallel)
- Lifting heels off the ground or shifting weight to toes
- Looking up or down instead of keeping the neck neutral
- Hips rising faster than shoulders (good-morning squat)
- Not bracing the core before each rep
- Using too much weight and sacrificing form

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Olympic Barbell (45 lbs/20 kg)
- Squat Rack or Power Rack
- Weight Plates
- Safety Bars or Spotter Arms (recommended)
- Optional: Lifting Belt (for heavy loads)
- Optional: Squat Shoes or Flat-soled Shoes
- Optional: Chalk (for grip)

sections.heading: Rack Setup
sections.content:
1. Set the J-hooks at upper chest height for easy unracking.
2. Set safety bars just below your bottom squat position.
3. Load the barbell evenly on both sides.
4. Use collars to secure the plates.
5. Clear the area around the rack of any obstacles.
6. Ensure you have enough space to step back and squat safely.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Bar Position: High bar (on traps) or Low bar (on rear delts).
2. Grip: Thumbless or full grip, hands as close together as comfortable.
3. Elbow Position: Down and back to create upper back tightness.
4. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed out 15-30 degrees.
5. Core: Take a deep breath and brace before each rep.
6. Head: Neutral position, eyes looking forward.
7. Chest: Up and proud throughout the movement.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Front Squat: Barbell held in front rack position, more quad emphasis
- Goblet Squat: Dumbbell or kettlebell held at chest level
- Bulgarian Split Squat: Single-leg squat variation
- Leg Press: Machine-based alternative for lower body
- Hack Squat: Machine squat variation with back support
- Box Squat: Squat to a box for depth control

sections.heading: Back Squat Variations
sections.content:
High Bar Back Squat: Bar on upper traps, more upright torso, quad emphasis
Low Bar Back Squat: Bar on rear delts, more hip hinge, glute/hamstring emphasis
Pause Squat: Pause at the bottom for strength development
Tempo Squat: Controlled eccentric for muscle building
Box Squat: Squat to a box for consistent depth
1.5 Rep Squat: Full rep plus half rep for extra time under tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Knee Issues: Try box squats or reduce depth, focus on form
Back Issues: Front squat, goblet squat, or leg press
Mobility Issues: Goblet squat, use squat shoes with elevated heels
No Barbell: Dumbbell goblet squat or Bulgarian split squat
Beginner: Start with bodyweight squats, progress to goblet squat first
Want More Challenge: Add pause reps, tempo work, or deficit squats
